picks.reason: With Bloodborne at S and Dark Souls III at A, this is FromSoftware's same stamina-and-punish combat stretched across a huge open world, which suits a long haul. The tone is bleak and cryptic, the bosses are brutal, and when you hit a wall you can ride off and explore somewhere else.
picks.caveat: The ≈53 h figure is a focused run; thorough exploration easily doubles it. The pacing is looser and less tightly curated than Bloodborne's dense level design.

picks.reason: This is the closest thing to Souls in 2D: a melancholy ruined kingdom, lore told through fragments, a corpse-run on death, and demanding pattern-based bosses. It should hit the same nerve as Bloodborne's atmosphere and difficulty. At about 45 h of slow-burn exploration it fits a long-haul slot well.
picks.caveat: The first few hours are slow and the map system is deliberately obtuse. It is precision platforming and nail combat, not 3D action.

picks.reason: It is a superbly crafted, joyful platformer, but nothing in your tier list points toward it. It is breezy, low-stakes and nearly frictionless, while your top ranks all favor dark tone and hard-won victories. It works best as a palate cleanser between punishing games, not as your main long-haul commitment.
picks.caveat: The main story is only about 12-15 h. The ≈45 h figure assumes moon-hunting completionism, and the difficulty stays gentle until the post-game.
